Toxic

/TAHk-sik/ — rhymes with logic · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Toxic describes something poisonous or harmful to living things.

Keep the toxic cleaning fluids locked away from children and pets.

Worked Example

A teenager opens an old storage shed and finds a pile of unlabeled bottles left by a previous owner. The fumes that leak out make her dizzy and her eyes water. She slams the door shut and runs outside, recognizing at once that whatever is inside that shed is toxic and unsafe to handle.

Toxic is more precise than 'dangerous' here because it specifically names the chemical or biological threat—the harm comes from poison or toxins, not from a general hazard like a sharp edge or slippery surface.

How Toxic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

harmful

harmful: causing damage or injury of any kind

poisonous

poisonous: containing poison that can sicken or kill

noxious

noxious: harmful or unwholesome, especially fumes or gases

Antonyms

benign

benign: gentle and doing no harm at all

harmless

harmless: unable to cause any injury or damage

How Strong Is It? — disagreeable → harmful → noxious → toxic

disagreeable vs. toxic

disagreeable vs. toxic: Disagreeable is far weaker than toxic; disagreeable is merely unpleasant, while toxic means actively poisonous and able to harm living things.

harmful vs. toxic

harmful vs. toxic: Harmful is broader and weaker than toxic; harmful covers any kind of damage, while toxic specifies poisonous harm to the body.

noxious vs. toxic

noxious vs. toxic: Noxious is close to toxic, but toxic is stronger; noxious means harmful or unwholesome, while toxic emphasizes outright poison strong enough to injure or kill.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tox-

Root — tox-: bow; arrow poison (Greek)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: pertaining to; having the nature of (Greek/Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Tox- named the poison smeared on arrow tips, and -ic means 'pertaining to,' so toxic literally means 'pertaining to poison' — describing anything poisonous or harmful to living things.

Use the root in a new word: intoxicated

Use the root in a new word: intoxicated: Someone who is intoxicated has taken in a toxic amount of alcohol; both words grow from the same 'poison' root.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral to formal

Toxic names poisonous or chemically harmful substances and their effects—a direct, serious word rooted in chemistry. Use it when describing poisons, contaminated air, or water. For general harm that isn't chemical or biological in nature, 'harmful' is simpler and more precise.
